title: EEG Record Review
description: This course is a practice in electroencephalograph (EEG) record review of normal adult and pediatric patients, and progresses to EEG record review of neurological patients. Technical description of normal EEG patterns lays the foundation for the remainder of the course. Emphasis is placed on abnormal EEG patterns, their classification and their correlation to clinical disorders. This course is designed for students enrolled in the Neurodiagnostic Technology Program.
outcomes: Students will be able to identify the characteristics of EEG recordings in technical terms, frequency, morphology, topography, and reactivity.
Students will be able to differentiate between normal and abnormal waveforms.
Students will be identify infective disorders, encephalopathies, abnormal lesions, and generalized epilepsy.
objectives: Describe the characteristics of EEG recordings in technical terms frequency, morphology, topography and reactivity.
Describe the general EEG characteristics of normal and abnormal waveforms in technical terms.
Compare and contrast normal and abnormal waveforms.
Identify and describe the following infective disorders, encephalopathies, space-occupying lesions and generalized epilepsy.
Identify and describe the following conditions: convulsive status, non-convulsive status, secondary bilateral synchrony and difference between primary and secondary epilepsy.
content: Symmetry of voltage & frequency between hemispheres
Manner of occurrence (continuous or intermittent, random or rhythmic)
Reactivity (with eye opening, sensory stimulation, etc.)
Consideration of characteristics of EEG recordings
Examination of whether the described characteristics are appropriate to the patient's EEG and state of consciousness
Stage I, II and III sleep
Atypical spike & wave - multiple or polyspike & wave
Focal spikes and sharp waves (interictal epileptiform discharges or IEDS)
Benign rolandic epilepsy (BRE) and benign epileptiform centrotemporal spikes (BECTS)

Bilateral independent periodic epileptiform discharges or BiPEDS (generalized periodic epileptiform discharges or GPEDs) and bilateral independent periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges or BiPLEDS
EEG in Infective Disorders and Encephalopathies (Toxic, Metabolic, Inflammatory, Hypoxic, Degenerative and Prion)
EEG in Focal Structural Lesions/Space-Occupying Lesions
assignments: Professional journals related to neurology and neurodiagnostic technology including: Journal of Clinical Neurophysiology and Neurodiagnostic Journal
Course textbook chapter readings and completion of chapter review questions
Homework assignment completion including review of EEG recordings
Describing electroencephalographic characteristics of normal and abnormal waveforms including frequency, morphology, topography and reactivity.
Identifying and describing various EEG patterns in normal and abnormal EEG recordings.
Creating an EEG atlas portfolio with examples and written descriptions of normal EEG patterns.
